Structured nonconstant shapes already beat the constant without any local search: edge-heavy/concave-up families reached 0.7086 (p0003) and a symmetric trapezoid with a central plateau and tapered edges reached 0.7238 (p0005), both at N=2000. The best shapes share a common signature: f*f is made flatter and broader (more knots near its maximum) and its peak is pushed off-center, which lowers ||f*f||_inf faster than it lowers ||f*f||_2^2. Resolution and search method trade off: the best score came at coarse N=50 (p0002, 0.833) while finer N=800-4000 hill-climbs plateaued lower (p0004 0.807, p0007 0.804). It is unclear whether coarse discretization itself helps (fewer degrees of freedom, smoother f*f) or whether the finer searches were simply less effective per unit budget; testing the same hill-climb at matched effective resolution

Systematic coordinate-wise multiplicative sweeps (multi-epsilon, accept-immediately) plus block-perturbation escapes and periodic multi-resolution kicks beat p0002's random-only block hill-climb on the same N=50 shape: 0.8329 -> 0.8523 (p0010). The gain comes from exploiting the existing coarse shape more thoroughly rather than searching a new one, confirming there was real headroom left at N=50.

A monotone gamma-warp of p0002's profile (area-averaging over warped knots) followed by the base block climb reached 0.8553 (p0008), the best of generation 2, from 0.8329. The warp stage acts as a real mechanism for reshaping the profile, not just a search kick; the winning shape ended with a centered f*f peak (0.50) and 14% zeros, so the earlier off-center peak was incidental rather than causal.

Finer-resolution climbs from p0002 itself (p0012 at N=200 -> 0.8497; p0009 at N=32000 -> 0.8391; p0011 at N=3200 -> 0.8432; p0013 at N=800 -> 0.8372) all landed below the N=50 coordinate search (p0010, 0.8523) and the N=50 warp (p0008, 0.8553). This is consistent with coarse N being advantageous, but each fine run used a different search method and budget, so whether N=50 is intrinsically special

A low-dimensional control-point representation (K=8-16 control values linearly interpolated to the step heights, optimized by Nelder-Mead with restarts, then block-perturbation polish) escapes the N=50 local basin that all local moves from p0008 keep returning to: from p0008 (0.8553) it reached 0.8597 (p0017), a +0.0044 gain, producing a smooth zero-free shape (0% zeros, max/mean 3.62) at N=200 wi

Progressive N escalation with area-average resampling plus a final extend stage of short restarts from the best-so-far, all sharing one global best, gave the generation's top score: from p0008 (0.8553) it reached 0.8669 (p0014) at N=400, a +0.0116 gain, with the f*f peak pushed strongly off-center (0.286). This shows that finer resolution does help when the search method is held fixed and the budg

Combining the two separately-proven operators on the same shape — alternating gamma-warp sweeps with coordinate-wise multiplicative sweeps and short block-perturbation escapes at N=50 — beats either alone: from p0008 (0.8553) it reached 0.8637 (p0019), a +0.0084 gain, confirming the warp and coordinate-sweep gains are complementary rather than redundant.

A controlled resolution sweep using the identical warp-then-block-climb method at each N (30-200) from p0008 returned its start unchanged after 22 s of a 25 s budget (p0018), so it is not evidence about whether N=50 is intrinsically special; the equal-slice budget left too little time per N for the change to act. It needs a larger budget or fewer N values to settle the question.
